biography.plain_text: Charles J. Cella was an American businessman from St. Louis and the third generation of his family to own and lead Oaklawn Park in Arkansas. He succeeded his father at the racetrack and also headed Southern Real Estate and Financial Company, which held commercial properties and shopping centres around St. Louis.

long_biography.plain_text:
Competition from nearby casinos pushed Oaklawn owner Charles Cella and his management team to find new ways to sustain horse racing. General manager Eric Jackson devised Instant Racing, which allowed customers to wager on replays of past races. Its introduction in 2000, followed by additional electronic games, helped revive the track’s finances.

Gaming revenue increased the money available for race prizes, attracting stronger fields and reinforcing Oaklawn’s place in the racing calendar. Cella also participated as a racehorse owner, maintaining a stable of thoroughbreds alongside his role running the venue. His Northern Spur won the Breeders’ Cup Turf in 1995.
